paragraphs.text: And he spake a parable unto them to the end that they ought always to pray, and not to faint;
paragraphs.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς πρὸς τὸ δεῖν πάντοτε προσεύχεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ μὴ ἐγκακεῖν,
paragraphs.translit: Elegen de parabolēn autois pros to dein pantote proseuchesthai autous kai mē enkakein,

paragraphs.text: saying, There was in a city a judge, who feared not God, and regarded not man:
paragraphs.original: λέγων· Κριτής τις ἦν ἔν τινι πόλει τὸν θεὸν μὴ φοβούμενος καὶ ἄνθρωπον μὴ ἐντρεπόμενος.
paragraphs.translit: legōn· Kritēs tis ēn en tini polei ton theon mē phoboumenos kai anthrōpon mē entrepomenos.

paragraphs.text: and there was a widow in that city; and she came oft unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.
paragraphs.original: χήρα δὲ ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσα· Ἐκδίκησόν με ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου μου.
paragraphs.translit: chēra de ēn en tē polei ekeinē kai ērcheto pros auton legousa· Ekdikēson me apo tou antidikou mou.

paragraphs.text: And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man;
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἐπὶ χρόνον, μετὰ ταῦτα δὲ εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ· Εἰ καὶ τὸν θεὸν οὐ φοβοῦμαι οὐδὲ ἄνθρωπον ἐντρέπομαι,
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk ēthelen epi chronon, meta tauta de eipen en heautō· Ei kai ton theon ou phoboumai oude anthrōpon entrepomai,

paragraphs.text: yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest she wear me out by her continual coming.
paragraphs.original: διά γε τὸ παρέχειν μοι κόπον τὴν χήραν ταύτην ἐκδικήσω αὐτήν, ἵνα μὴ εἰς τέλος ἐρχομένη ὑπωπιάζῃ με.
paragraphs.translit: dia ge to parechein moi kopon tēn chēran tautēn ekdikēsō autēn, hina mē eis telos erchomenē hypōpiazē me.

paragraphs.text: And the Lord said, Hear what the unrighteous judge saith.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος· Ἀκούσατε τί ὁ κριτὴς τῆς ἀδικίας λέγει·
paragraphs.translit: eipen de ho kyrios· Akousate ti ho kritēs tēs adikias legei·

paragraphs.text: And shall not God avenge his elect, that cry to him day and night, and [yet] he is longsuffering over them?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ θεὸς οὐ μὴ ποιήσῃ τὴν ἐκδίκησιν τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ τῶν βοώντων αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, καὶ μακροθυμεῖ ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς;
paragraphs.translit: ho de theos ou mē poiēsē tēn ekdikēsin tōn eklektōn autou tōn boōntōn autō hēmeras kai nyktos, kai makrothymei epʼ autois;

paragraphs.text: I say unto you, that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?
paragraphs.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ποιήσει τὴν ἐκδίκησιν αὐτῶν ἐν τάχει. πλὴν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐλθὼν ἆρα εὑρήσει τὴν πίστιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;
paragraphs.translit: legō hymin hoti poiēsei tēn ekdikēsin autōn en tachei. plēn ho hyios tou anthrōpou elthōn ara heurēsei tēn pistin epi tēs gēs;

paragraphs.text: And he spake also this parable unto certain who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and set all others at nought:
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ πρός τινας τοὺς πεποιθότας ἐφʼ ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι εἰσὶν δίκαιοι καὶ ἐξουθενοῦντας τοὺς λοιποὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην·
paragraphs.translit: Eipen de kai pros tinas tous pepoithotas ephʼ heautois hoti eisin dikaioi kai exouthenountas tous loipous tēn parabolēn tautēn·

paragraphs.text: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.
paragraphs.original: Ἄνθρωποι δύο ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσεύξασθαι, ὁ εἷς Φαρισαῖος καὶ ὁ ἕτερος τελώνης.
paragraphs.translit: Anthrōpoi dyo anebēsan eis to hieron proseuxasthai, ho heis Pharisaios kai ho heteros telōnēs.

paragraphs.text: The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as the rest of men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican.
paragraphs.original: ὁ Φαρισαῖος σταθεὶς πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ταῦτα προσηύχετο· Ὁ θεός, εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὥσπερ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἅρπαγες, ἄδικοι, μοιχοί, ἢ καὶ ὡς οὗτος ὁ τελώνης·
paragraphs.translit: ho Pharisaios statheis pros heauton tauta prosēucheto· Ho theos, eucharistō soi hoti ouk eimi hōsper hoi loipoi tōn anthrōpōn, harpages, adikoi, moichoi, ē kai hōs houtos ho telōnēs·

paragraphs.text: I fast twice in the week; I give tithes of all that I get.
paragraphs.original: νηστεύω δὶς τοῦ σαββάτου, ἀποδεκατῶ πάντα ὅσα κτῶμαι.
paragraphs.translit: nēsteuō dis tou sabbatou, apodekatō panta hosa ktōmai.

paragraphs.text: But the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote his breast, saying, God, be thou merciful to me a sinner.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ τελώνης μακρόθεν ἑστὼς οὐκ ἤθελεν οὐδὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἐπᾶραι εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, ἀλλʼ ἔτυπτε τὸ στῆθος αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ὁ θεός, ἱλάσθητί μοι τῷ ἁμαρτωλῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de telōnēs makrothen hestōs ouk ēthelen oude tous ophthalmous eparai eis ton ouranon, allʼ etypte to stēthos autou legōn· Ho theos, hilasthēti moi tō hamartōlō.

paragraphs.text: I say unto you, This man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled; but he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
paragraphs.original: λέγω ὑμῖν, κατέβη οὗτος δεδικαιωμένος εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ παρʼ ἐκεῖνον· ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: legō hymin, katebē houtos dedikaiōmenos eis ton oikon autou parʼ ekeinon· hoti pas ho hypsōn heauton tapeinōthēsetai, ho de tapeinōn heauton hypsōthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: And they were bringing unto him also their babes, that he should touch them: but when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
paragraphs.original: Προσέφερον δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ τὰ βρέφη ἵνα αὐτῶν ἅπτηται· ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Prosepheron de autō kai ta brephē hina autōn haptētai· idontes de hoi mathētai epetimōn autois.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus called them unto him, saying, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for to such belongeth the kingdom of God.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσεκαλέσατο αὐτὰ λέγων· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με καὶ μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous prosekalesato auta legōn· Aphete ta paidia erchesthai pros me kai mē kōlyete auta, tōn gar toioutōn estin hē basileia tou theou.

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall in no wise enter therein.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin, hos an mē dexētai tēn basileian tou theou hōs paidion, ou mē eiselthē eis autēn.

paragraphs.text: And a certain ruler asked him, saying, Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησέν τις αὐτὸν ἄρχων λέγων· Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;
paragraphs.translit: Kai epērōtēsen tis auton archōn legōn· Didaskale agathe, ti poiēsas zōēn aiōnion klēronomēsō;

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? none is good, save one, [even] God.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν; οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de autō ho Iēsous· Ti me legeis agathon; oudeis agathos ei mē heis ho theos.

paragraphs.text: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honor thy father and mother.
paragraphs.original: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας· Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς, Μὴ φονεύσῃς, Μὴ κλέψῃς, Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα.
paragraphs.translit: tas entolas oidas· Mē moicheusēs, Mē phoneusēs, Mē klepsēs, Mē pseudomartyrēsēs, Tima ton patera sou kai tēn mētera.

paragraphs.text: And he said, All these things have I observed from my youth up.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ταῦτα πάντα ἐφύλαξα ἐκ νεότητος μου.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Tauta panta ephylaxa ek neotētos mou.

paragraphs.text: And when Jesus heard it, he said unto him, One thing thou lackest yet: sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἔτι ἕν σοι λείπει· πάντα ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ διάδος πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.
paragraphs.translit: akousas de ho Iēsous eipen autō· Eti hen soi leipei· panta hosa echeis pōlēson kai diados ptōchois, kai hexeis thēsauron en ouranois, kai deuro akolouthei moi.

paragraphs.text: But when he heard these things, he became exceeding sorrowful; for he was very rich.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας ταῦτα περίλυπος ἐγενήθη, ἦν γὰρ πλούσιος σφόδρα.
paragraphs.translit: ho de akousas tauta perilypos egenēthē, ēn gar plousios sphodra.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus seeing him said, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!
paragraphs.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσπορεύονται·
paragraphs.translit: Idōn de auton ho Iēsous eipen· Pōs dyskolōs hoi ta chrēmata echontes eis tēn basileian tou theou eisporeuontai·

paragraphs.text: For it is easier for a camel to enter in through a needle`s eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
paragraphs.original: εὐκοπώτερον γάρ ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τρήματος βελόνης εἰσελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: eukopōteron gar estin kamēlon dia trēmatos belonēs eiselthein ē plousion eis tēn basileian tou theou eiselthein.

paragraphs.text: And they that heard it said, Then who can be saved?
paragraphs.original: Εἶπαν δὲ οἱ ἀκούσαντες· Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι;
paragraphs.translit: Eipan de hoi akousantes· Kai tis dynatai sōthēnai;

paragraphs.text: But he said, The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Τὰ ἀδύνατα παρὰ ἀνθρώποις δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Ta adynata para anthrōpois dynata para tō theō estin.

paragraphs.text: And Peter said, Lo, we have left our own, and followed thee.
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφέντες τὰ ἴδια ἠκολουθήσαμέν σοι.
paragraphs.translit: Eipen de ho Petros· Idou hēmeis aphentes ta idia ēkolouthēsamen soi.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or wife, or brethren, or parents, or children, for the kingdom of God`s sake,
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ γυναῖκα ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ γονεῖς ἢ τέκνα ἕνεκεν τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autois· Amēn legō hymin hoti oudeis estin hos aphēken oikian ē gynaika ē adelphous ē goneis ē tekna heneken tēs basileias tou theou,

paragraphs.text: who shall not receive manifold more in this time, and in the world to come eternal life.
paragraphs.original: ὃς οὐχὶ μὴ ἀπολάβῃ πολλαπλασίονα ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
paragraphs.translit: hos ouchi mē apolabē pollaplasiona en tō kairō toutō kai en tō aiōni tō erchomenō zōēn aiōnion.

paragraphs.text: And he took unto him the twelve, and said unto them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all the things that are written through the prophets shall be accomplished unto the Son of man.
paragraphs.original: Παραλαβὼν δὲ τοὺς δώδεκα εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, καὶ τελεσθήσεται πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα διὰ τῶν προφητῶν τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
paragraphs.translit: Paralabōn de tous dōdeka eipen pros autous· Idou anabainomen eis Ierousalēm, kai telesthēsetai panta ta gegrammena dia tōn prophētōn tō hyiō tou anthrōpou·

paragraphs.text: For he shall be delivered up unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and shamefully treated, and spit upon:
paragraphs.original: παραδοθήσεται γὰρ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ ἐμπαιχθήσεται καὶ ὑβρισθήσεται καὶ ἐμπτυσθήσεται,
paragraphs.translit: paradothēsetai gar tois ethnesin kai empaichthēsetai kai hybristhēsetai kai emptysthēsetai,

paragraphs.text: and they shall scourge and kill him: and the third day he shall rise again.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μαστιγώσαντες ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ ἀναστήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai mastigōsantes apoktenousin auton, kai tē hēmera tē tritē anastēsetai.

paragraphs.text: And they understood none of these things; and this saying was hid from them, and they perceived not the things that were said.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐδὲν τούτων συνῆκαν, καὶ ἦν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο κεκρυμμένον ἀπʼ αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκον τὰ λεγόμενα.
paragraphs.translit: kai autoi ouden toutōn synēkan, kai ēn to rhēma touto kekrymmenon apʼ autōn, kai ouk eginōskon ta legomena.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, as he drew nigh unto Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way side begging:
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἐγγίζειν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰεριχὼ τυφλός τις ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἐπαιτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de en tō engizein auton eis Ierichō typhlos tis ekathēto para tēn hodon epaitōn.

paragraphs.text: and hearing a multitude going by, he inquired what this meant.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσας δὲ ὄχλου διαπορευομένου ἐπυνθάνετο τί εἴη τοῦτο·
paragraphs.translit: akousas de ochlou diaporeuomenou epynthaneto ti eiē touto·

paragraphs.text: And they told him that Jesus of Nazareth passeth by.
paragraphs.original: ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος παρέρχεται.
paragraphs.translit: apēngeilan de autō hoti Iēsous ho Nazōraios parerchetai.

paragraphs.text: And he cried, saying, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐβόησεν λέγων· Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.
paragraphs.translit: kai eboēsen legōn· Iēsou hyie Dauid, eleēson me.

paragraphs.text: And they that went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried out the more a great deal, Thou son of David, have mercy on me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἱ προάγοντες ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ ἵνα σιγήσῃ· αὐτὸς δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν· Υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi proagontes epetimōn autō hina sigēsē· autos de pollō mallon ekrazen· Hyie Dauid, eleēson me.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus stood, and commanded him to be brought unto him: and when he was come near, he asked him,
paragraphs.original: σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ἀχθῆναι πρὸς αὐτόν. ἐγγίσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: statheis de ho Iēsous ekeleusen auton achthēnai pros auton. engisantos de autou epērōtēsen auton·

paragraphs.text: What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? And he said, Lord, that I may receive my sight.
paragraphs.original: Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω.
paragraphs.translit: Ti soi theleis poiēsō; ho de eipen· Kyrie, hina anablepsō.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto him, Receive thy sight; thy faith hath made thee whole.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀνάβλεψον· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho Iēsous eipen autō· Anablepson· hē pistis sou sesōken se.

paragraphs.text: And immediately he received his sight, and followed him, glorifying God: and all the people, when they saw it, gave praise unto God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνέβλεψεν, καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ δοξάζων τὸν θεόν. καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἰδὼν ἔδωκεν αἶνον τῷ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai parachrēma aneblepsen, kai ēkolouthei autō doxazōn ton theon. kai pas ho laos idōn edōken ainon tō theō.
